name: Stephanie Gao
about:
Stephanie Gao
Hi, I’m Steph. I study computer science and cognitive science at Minerva University.
I build tools that make tech feel a little more whimsical. I worked in product and growth at Dedalus Labs. Before that, I was CPO of my app Matcha, which got acquired, and a technical project manager at Axlora, a compliance company acquired by Cognition.
Outside of that: dance, hiking, makeup, content creation, and rom-coms.

projects.name: Aura Protection
projects.description: Aura Protection is a concept for making attention boundaries visible instead of burying them in settings. The interaction centers on a small, playful pause before a distracting action. The interesting product challenge is designing an interruption that feels helpful without becoming another distraction.
projects.tags: Product concept · Interaction design · Attention UX

projects.name: Automata Lab
projects.description: Automata Lab is a JavaScript workbench for editing DFA, NFA, and PDA diagrams and inspecting their computation trees. It supports step-by-step exploration, explicit epsilon transitions, and PNG, SVG, or clipboard export. A question importer can prepare an editable draft from pasted ChatGPT JSON; direct image recognition still requires separate AI setup.
projects.tags: JavaScript · DFA/NFA/PDA · Computation trees · Export

projects.name: Beacon
projects.description: Beacon is an academic concept for tsunami preparedness and response. It organizes hazard information into a short sequence of actions so a person can find the next step under time pressure. The technical design challenge is prioritizing location, alert state, and offline access without making the emergency interface harder to scan.
projects.tags: Emergency UX · Information architecture · Offline-first design

projects.name: BFFR
projects.description: BFFR is a digital reality-check concept with a deliberately direct voice. It turns a moment of overthinking into a short prompt to reconsider an assumption. The design experiment is how much personality an interface can have while still giving people a clear, useful interaction.
projects.tags: Product concept · Conversational UX · Voice design

projects.name: Buenos Aires Climate Refuges
projects.description: Buenos Aires Climate Refuges is a bilingual React and TypeScript prototype for finding climate shelters and drinking fountains. It searches a local dataset of 269 shelters and 176 fountains with filters and record details. An optional Google Maps layer adds map selection and walking directions; the core search works without an API key. The app has no backend or account system.
projects.tags: React · TypeScript · Geospatial search · Bilingual UX

projects.name: Bulby
projects.description: Bulby is an Electron desktop overlay that transcribes microphone and call audio locally with faster-whisper. I connected the live transcript and a fresh screenshot to a Chrome extension that hands context to ChatGPT only when the user asks. The compact window can expand, move, and resize; the local transcription path needs no OpenAI API key.
projects.tags: Electron · TypeScript · faster-whisper · Chrome extension

projects.name: Caba
projects.description: Caba is an academic product concept for simplifying a complicated workflow. The proposed interface breaks information into smaller decisions and makes progress visible. Its technical focus is information architecture: deciding what the tool needs to store, what the user must enter, and what can be deferred.
projects.tags: Information architecture · Workflow design · Prototyping

projects.name: Caughtcha
projects.description: Caughtcha is a small JavaScript experiment about noticing online habits in the moment. It uses a well-timed interruption as the central interaction rather than a dashboard of retrospective statistics. The interesting design constraint is making the prompt noticeable without making it disruptive.
projects.tags: JavaScript · Interaction design · Behavioral UX

projects.name: Christmas Lights
projects.description: Christmas Lights is an interactive seasonal screen experiment built in JavaScript. Instead of a static holiday image, it treats light and motion as the interface. The project is a small study in timing, visual feedback, and making a browser feel like an object in a room.
projects.tags: JavaScript · Motion design · Creative coding

projects.name: Cyber for Students
projects.description: Cyber for Students taught command-line and networking fundamentals across 16 countries. I provisioned dedicated Linux virtual machines so learners could practice in their own environments. The curriculum used 250 custom capture-the-flag challenges, turning shell and security concepts into problems students could solve hands-on.
projects.tags: Linux VMs · CLI · Networking · CTF design

projects.name: DelusionGPT
projects.description: DelusionGPT is a TypeScript command-line companion for stressed developers. It uses Commander and Inquirer for the terminal flow and Chalk for its intentionally theatrical responses. The interesting constraint is expressing a distinct personality through text, prompts, and timing instead of a graphical interface.
projects.tags: TypeScript · Node.js · Commander · Inquirer

projects.name: ÉVOLUER
projects.description: ÉVOLUER is a L’Oréal Brandstorm fragrance concept built around one base scent that changes through the seasons. We designed a spray-count mechanism for releasing monthly scent capsules and mapped the experience from bottle use to an in-store Fragrance Observatory. The work combined product mechanics, scent-journey prototyping, and brand design; it won the Japan national round in 2026.
projects.tags: Product mechanics · Prototyping · Brand design

projects.name: Green Carbon
projects.description: Green Carbon is a working field-mapping and farmer-logbook prototype. It uses Leaflet for polygon drawing and overlap checks, Supabase for profile and field data, and local storage as a fallback when the service is unavailable. The workflow links boundary geometry to activity records so farm verification is easier to inspect, including in low-connectivity settings.
projects.tags: Leaflet · Supabase · Geospatial data · Offline fallback

projects.name: Homework Hound
projects.description: Homework Hound is a Chrome extension that sends a pixel dog across the current page to “eat” the homework. JavaScript controls the dog’s appetite, the page effect, stopping, and cleanup so the interaction is reversible. It can also export an evidence.png screenshot of the joke.
projects.tags: JavaScript · Chrome extension · DOM interaction

projects.name: Instagram Follow Checker
projects.description: Instagram Follow Checker compares followers and following from Instagram exports entirely in the browser. It reads multiple ZIPs or extracted JSON/HTML, combines numbered follower files, and deduplicates usernames before showing searchable results. The ZIP parser handles stored and deflated entries, including ZIP64, without an account, server upload, or installation.
projects.tags: Client-side ZIP parsing · JSON/HTML · Search UI

projects.name: Lockin Twin
projects.description: Lockin Twin is a focus-companion app built with React and TypeScript. Its repository uses MediaPipe Face Mesh for camera-based face tracking and Framer Motion for interface animation. The technical experiment is whether a responsive character can make the start of a work session feel less solitary.
projects.tags: React · TypeScript · MediaPipe Face Mesh · Framer Motion

projects.name: Matcha (acquired)
projects.description: Matcha turned handwritten notes into AI flashcards and practice tests for active recall. As CPO, I led product decisions, branding, and growth while shaping the note-to-study workflow. It reached 320 active users in its first month and was acquired for integration into a productivity-app suite.
projects.tags: AI study tools · Product strategy · Growth

projects.name: Minerva Marketplace
projects.description: Minerva Marketplace is a peer-to-peer marketplace designed for a student community of about 1,000 across international rotations; that is the target community, not a claimed active-user count. I designed PostgreSQL schemas for users and listings, implemented OAuth, and set up scheduled email notifications. The interesting systems problem is keeping listings and transactions useful as students change cities each semester.
projects.tags: PostgreSQL · OAuth · Scheduled email

projects.name: Mymizu
projects.description: Mymizu is a React prototype for making water refills easier to find and repeat. The consumer side combines a Google Maps refill map, daily refill tracking, and a growing sprout companion; an admin view diagnoses underserved “red zones” and suggests new stations. I explored how geospatial analysis, reminders, and small rewards can connect individual behavior to network coverage.
projects.tags: React · Google Maps · Geospatial analysis · Behavioral design

projects.name: Preclass
projects.description: Preclass is a Manifest V3 Chrome and Edge extension for Minerva Forum. It collects readings or numbered workbook questions into a reviewable prompt and sends it to a chosen ChatGPT course conversation. The workbook collector checks for missing questions; the handoff preserves existing drafts and offers a copy fallback. It runs without a backend, API key, analytics, or inference billing.
projects.tags: JavaScript · Manifest V3 · DOM extraction · Browser automation

projects.name: seen.
projects.description: seen. is a TypeScript and Next.js experiment built around the feeling of being left on read. Its repository includes React, an OpenRouter integration, and scripts for iMessage interaction. The interesting technical question is how to turn a familiar messaging signal into a responsive experience rather than a static joke.
projects.tags: Next.js · TypeScript · React · OpenRouter

projects.name: Setlist Gym Log
projects.description: Setlist is a weekly gym dashboard that stores workout entries in the browser. It records start and end times, tracks exercises by day, and attaches up to eight photos per session. Weekly duration and session totals are calculated automatically, and the displayed week can be exported as CSV.
projects.tags: Browser storage · Photo attachments · Duration calculation · CSV export

projects.name: Speakeasy Terminal
projects.description: Speakeasy Terminal is a concept for a hidden space navigated through typed commands. It treats command parsing, discoverability, and feedback as the experience rather than hiding them behind conventional menus. The design challenge is making a terminal feel inviting to someone who has never used one.
projects.tags: Command UX · Interaction design · Information architecture

projects.name: Twin
projects.description: Twin is a concept for a digital counterpart shaped by a person’s preferences and repeated interactions. It explores what the interface would need to remember to feel consistent over time. The technical product question is how to make that state legible and editable, so personalization stays understandable.
projects.tags: Personalization · State design · Product concept

projects.name: Vectorizer
projects.description: Vectorizer converts images and video frames into 50 × 50 grayscale matrices for a linear-algebra exploration. A Python CLI can export CSV, JSON, or Sage-compatible matrix text, while a Flask app processes uploaded images and clips. I varied epsilon thresholds and replayed processed frames to inspect information loss and motion continuity.
projects.tags: Python · Flask · Image processing · Linear algebra

projects.name: Yuki Issei
projects.description: Yuki Issei combined a musician’s web presence, visual identity, and short-form content. I built the site, edited clips and a lyric video, designed the poster, and coordinated the production workflow. AI-assisted song drafts became a starting point for human vocal recordings with the singer.
projects.tags: Web development · Video editing · Creative production
